name: mangos-recoverable-protocol-context-shutdown
instr:
Mangos lacks recoverable context shutdown with terminal accounting for every accepted message. Add an idempotent terminal transition that stops admission and either returns unresolved work immediately or awaits bounded settlement across raw queue, request/reply, survey, and respondent protocols, without changing ordinary context behavior.

Concurrent shutdowns must return equivalent accounting without deadlock, duplicate ownership transfers, or operations owned twice. Give each accepted message one disposition. Returned messages transfer exclusively and intact; settled and discarded messages never transfer.

XPAIR, XPAIR1, and XBUS must preserve peer, replacement, receive, broadcast-clone, and exclusion semantics while reporting application outcomes once. Distinguish queued from pipe-accepted work in XPAIR and XPAIR1. Return unresolved work with original bodies and headers. Peer loss is not settlement; in XPAIR1 it returns unresolved work and releases a blocked receiver without hiding a delivered message. Partial XBUS fan-out yields one ownership-safe application item, consistent counts, and no transferred transport clones.

Raw XREQ and XREP preserve unresolved protocol headers and clear routing associations before completion. Each REQ request gets one ownership-safe terminal outcome across queued admission, retransmission, and replies on either side of the shutdown boundary. REP and RESPONDENT retain reply affinity only while delivery is possible. SURVEYOR deterministically
